about: The Node.js the stage copies into the app (bundle.mjs checkNode) and every job of the release workflow runs: this exact version, the official build (the Node.js project’s own download). `tarballs`: the sha256 of each platform’s official tarball, as the project’s SHASUMS256.txt for the version lists it — the release workflow downloads it, checks it against that sum before anything of it is unpacked or run, and installs it (apps/desktop/scripts/ci-node.sh: darwin-arm64 on the macOS jobs, linux-x64 on the ubuntu ones). `sha256`: the sha256 of that tarball’s bin/node — ci-node.sh checks it once unpacked, and the build refuses any other binary. Upgrading: take the new version’s SHASUMS256.txt and its signature (SHASUMS256.txt.asc) from the Node.js project, check the signature against a releaser key the project lists, record the version and each platform’s node-v<version>-<platform>.tar.gz line here, then download each tarball, check it against that line, and record `shasum -a 256 <extracted>/bin/node` for each platform.
